name: Moth The
overview: Scripture uses the image of the moth to illustrate the fragility and destruction inherent in earthly things and human folly, particularly in the context of God's judgments. The moth consumes garments, symbolizing how severe divine judgment can destroy what seems secure, as seen in Job's depiction of houses and garments eaten by moths (Job 4:19; 13:28; 27:18). Isaiah emphasizes that those opposed to God will deteriorate like old garments consumed by moths, while God's righteousness endures eternally (Isaiah 50:9; 51:8). Hosea further portrays God Himself as a moth bringing judgment and decay to unfaithful Israel (Hosea 5:12). This imagery underscores the transient nature of worldly security contrasted with the everlasting nature of God's salvation.
